Title: MCP Architecture | Model Context Protocol Architecture | CampusX
Description:
In this video, we dive deep into the Model Context Protocol (MCP) Architecture and break it down from first principles. 

We’ll cover:

The core building blocks of MCP → Host, Client, and Server
How they communicate and why the Client is essential
Real-world examples (GitHub, Slack, Google Drive)
The power of primitives: Tools, Resources, and Prompts
Standard operations like tools/list, resources/read, and more
The role of the Data Layer (JSON-RPC 2.0) and why it’s better than REST
The Transport Layer and how messages actually move between systems

By the end of this video, you’ll have a crystal-clear understanding of how MCP enables AI chatbots to seamlessly connect with external tools, scale across multiple services, and maintain safe, decoupled communication.

Title: The MCP Lifecycle | MCP Trilogy | CampusX
Description:
In this video, we continue our MCP (Model Context Protocol) playlist. So far, we’ve covered why MCP is needed and its architecture in detail. Today, we’ll move one step further and explore a very important concept – the MCP Life Cycle.

You’ll learn:

1. What an MCP session is and how it works
2. The three main stages of the MCP Life Cycle: Initialization, Normal Operation, and Shutdown
3. A step-by-step breakdown of how a host, client, and server interact during a session
4. Key rules you must follow during initialization to avoid errors
5. How version negotiation and capability negotiation take place
6. A practical demo using Claude Desktop and a File System server to show you how the process works behind the scenes with JSON-RPC messages

This concept is not just theory – it’s the foundation for when we start coding our own servers and clients later in the series.

Title: How to Build Local MCP Servers | MCP Trilogy | CampusX
Description:
Code - https://github.com/campusx-official/expense-tracker-mcp-server
Quick Revision -  https://docs.google.com/document/d/1xLHPVi07Jy3vZUjDNnC7BivUpN1Ro0aYDxP09yD3pzs/edit?usp=sharing

In this video, we continue our MCP (Model Context Protocol) playlist and show you how to build your own MCP server from scratch. We focus on creating a local Expense Tracker MCP server that can integrate with chatbot clients like Clot Desktop, so you can manage expenses using natural language commands.

You’ll see how to:
Set up the environment and install dependencies
Write and run Python code with FastMCP (a beginner-friendly layer over the MCP SDK)
Create MCP tools like add, list, and summarize expenses
Connect the server with Clot Desktop for real interaction
Debug using MCP Inspector
Store and manage expenses with an SQLite database
Add features like date-range filtering and category consistency

Along the way, we explain the MCP ecosystem, the difference between the official SDK and FastMCP, and why FastMCP makes development easier. We also show how to enforce categories with JSON resources and even convert a FastAPI app into an MCP server — a big advantage for businesses building multi-platform apps.

By the end of this tutorial, you’ll have a working expense tracker MCP server and a clear roadmap to turn it into a production-ready remote server.

What you’ll learn in this video:

Running and debugging your server with MCP Inspector
